Definition: {properly, something slaughtered; hence, a beast (or meat, as butchered); abstractly butchery (or concretely, a place of slaughter)}
BiblicalUsage: In Scripture, ṭibchâh is the word for slaughtered meat, butchery. In 1 Samuel 25:11, Shall I then take my bread, and it appears again in Psalms 44:22.
TheologicalSignificance: Meat set aside for a feast and a people counted as sheep for the slaughter both remind me that God sees His own, even when the world prices them like livestock.
